gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a 100 × 100 mm fill engrave at 0.1 mm line spacing takes at least about 4.2 minutes on the Bambu Lab H2D 10 W laser (400 mm/s) and at least about 16.7 minutes on the Snapmaker Artisan 10 W laser (100 mm/s). The two machines cost almost the same today: $1,949 for the H2D combo and $1,799 for the Artisan.
standout_why: I compared against desktop3dprinters.us/topics/3d-printer-laser-combos (the page cited in chat 1), desktop3dprinters.us/lists/3d-printers-with-laser-engraver (rank 1, not cited) and 3dengr.com/best-3d-printers-with-laser-engraver (cited in both chats). The cited combos page already works out Bambu's laser price premium ($600 for 10 W, $1,300 for 40 W, using launch prices) and its cost per watt ($60/W and $32.50/W). Any per-watt or premium figure from me would add nothing, so I left those out. The rank-1 list page gives Bambu's 400 and 1,000 mm/s engraving speeds. It does not give a speed for the Artisan's laser, and it never turns speed into job time. 3dengr gives no speeds, areas or prices for any model. None of the three pages compares engraving time, or laser area per dollar at today's prices, between the two machines ChatGPT ranked at the top.
decides: This splits the pick by use case and supports ChatGPT's order with numbers. For someone who mostly engraves, the H2D 10 W combo goes about 4 times faster at top speed for $150 more. The Artisan's laser covers about twice the area for $150 less (1,600 cm² vs 837 cm²) and also includes CNC. So it wins on large flat jobs and carving, not on speed.
